capabilities.justification: The CLI reads caller-selected manifests and reports plus repository metadata and source files for benchmark subjects.
The CLI creates caller-selected result directories and temporary worktree and staging directories.
The CLI writes result reports, samples, trials, logs, copied manifests, staged replay exports, and subject build outputs.
The CLI removes its temporary staging and worktree directories and cleans a newly reserved replay output directory after a failed export.
Runs git, host metadata commands, shells, and user-selected subject preparation, build, and service commands.
Stops the exact child process trees it starts after commands, services, or benchmark runs finish or fail.
Reads clocks for timestamps, benchmark durations, deadlines, and service readiness.
Sleeps for bounded readiness polling, workload hold intervals, and configured cooldowns.
Allocates an ephemeral loopback port for benchmark service subjects.
Probes and drives services at the address constructed from the tool's own loopback listener and allocated port.
On Windows the process-tree manager resolves fixed kernel32 job-object functions.
On Windows the process-tree manager calls fixed kernel32 job-object functions to assign and stop child trees.
The Unix process-tree cleanup starts one goroutine to forward termination notifications and stop live child trees.
The Unix signal-forwarder goroutine receives termination notifications over its channel.
Each started TCP service gets a goroutine that waits for its command to exit.
The service-waiter goroutine sends command completion through the service done channel to the caller.
Parallel TCP/RESP workloads start bounded client goroutines controlled by a semaphore.
The workload caller and bounded client goroutines coordinate through the semaphore and wait group.
The CLI reports help, status, result paths, and errors to standard output streams.

justification: The whole CLI accepts caller-selected filesystem paths and subject commands, creates benchmark and temporary outputs, measures and sleeps, and runs only its own loopback TCP services. Windows process-tree cleanup calls fixed kernel32 APIs. No direct environment-variable read or non-loopback network destination is present in the Go implementation.
